findings.problem: The brief plans an asset that can't be built. The instructions allow only pickers and troubleshooters and say not to plan diagrams.
findings.suggestion: Drop the diagram. Carry the burr direction (toward FINE) in the text or as one step of the troubleshooter.

findings.problem: All three title options break the 70-character limit, by a lot.
findings.evidence: "Barista Express or Pro still too fast at grind setting 1? Check these in order before buying a grinder" (~102 chars); "Breville built-in grinder won't go fine enough: a step-by-step fix, from beans to upper burr" (~92); "Fix the Barista Express grinder you have: beans, basket, dose, then the upper burr" (~83). They also read as summaries, where the instructions ask for one promise.
findings.suggestion: Count characters with product names filled in and cut each title to one promise, e.g. "Barista Express still fast at setting 1? Don't buy a grinder yet".

findings.problem: There were more competitor summaries than pages the agent actually opened in the run. The instructions say to fetch each of the top 3 pages, so some summaries probably came from the research artifact or from memory.
findings.evidence: recentRuns 2026-11-24T20:11: 3 fetches, 2 failed (brewcoffeehome 525, baristalife 404), so 1 page opened, yet 3 competitors were reviewed. Run 2026-11-25T13:59: 2 fetches and 0 failures, yet 3 competitors were reviewed. I spot-checked Appliances Online and Coffee Chronicler and both summaries were accurate, so this is a process gap, not a misdescription.
findings.suggestion: When a fetch fails, fetch the next search result instead. If a summary comes from the research artifact and not from a fetch made in this run, label it that way in competitorsReviewed.

findings.problem: Two theses say more than their own briefs support. Item 4's thesis uses a price multiple that its leaveOut bans. Item 3's thesis says the UK Express 'never asks for a descale', but its mustInclude says newer UK units may have the US-style light.
findings.evidence: thesis: "Before you spend two to three times your Barista Express..." vs leaveOut: "Prices and the 'two to three times' figure as a number." Thesis: "except the UK Express, which never asks for a descale" vs mustInclude: "newer UK units may have the US-style light, so readers should go by the label they actually see".
findings.suggestion: Before returning, check the thesis against leaveOut and mustInclude. The writer starts from the thesis, so it must not carry anything the brief tells them to cut.

findings.problem: The same free-checks gate (roast date, tamper-cap dose, burr cleaning, one upper-burr step) is written out in full in three briefs. The later posts risk repeating the diagnosis guide instead of building on it.
findings.evidence: Item 2's contributionDetail repeats all four gate steps and also reuses grind-fault-tree. Item 4 repeats the beans and dose test. Item 1 is the guide that owns this diagnosis.
findings.suggestion: When existingContent or a sibling brief already owns a diagnosis, reduce it to one line plus the {{guide:}} link or the shared tool, and spend the brief on what this post decides.

findings.problem: The brief hands an unverified fact to the writer, who has no way to check it, but still lists the supporting claim as supported.
findings.evidence: mustInclude: "Ask the writer to check the dosing-cup size before publishing, since the 2026-11-24 page read didn't show it", while claimIds includes baratza-encore-esp/us-dosing-cup.
findings.suggestion: If a page read didn't confirm a claim, leave it out or move it to leaveOut as unknown. Don't hand verification to the writer.

findings.problem: The rule for Barista Pro owners rests on something the booklet doesn't say, while the same brief marks the Pro's ability to brew and steam at once as unknown.
findings.evidence: "its booklet describes no wait for steam, so a Pro owner's case for a dual boiler on steaming grounds is weaker" vs leaveOut: "Any claim that the Oracle Jet or Barista Pro can or can't brew and steam at the same time. Both are unknown."
findings.suggestion: Base branch decisions on documented claims (here, the 3-second ThermoJet heat-up). Present any inference as editorial judgement, not as a fact from the booklet.

findings.problem: Search coverage is thin: every recent run made exactly one search.
findings.evidence: recentRuns: searches = 1 in all three runs. Home-Barista returned 403, and brewcoffeehome and baristalife failed.
findings.suggestion: Run a second search using the reader's own wording (or a forum/Reddit phrasing) so the top-3 set isn't decided by one query, and replace any page that fails to load.

summary: A strong batch. All four briefs have a real thesis an owner can act on, an honest keep-yours default, a careful line between what is documented and what isn't, and accurate competitor summaries: all three pages I spot-checked say what the briefs claim. The main fix is to make the agent check its hard constraints before returning. One brief plans a diagram, which can't be built, and every title in that brief is over 70 characters. Two runs reviewed three competitors after only one or two successful fetches.
keep: The thesis is an actionable opinion with 'keep yours / buy nothing' as the default outcome, and it names the smallest sensible purchase when the free fixes fail.

An explicit 'what the source doesn't say' handling: unknowns such as the factory burr position, burr range, reset procedure and invented intervals are named and sent to leaveOut instead of being guessed.

Competitor summaries are specific and accurate, and they name a concrete gap for this reader. The Seattle Coffee Gear 'adjust the burr coarser', Appliances Online light and Coffee Chronicler grinder/IMS claims all checked out.
Market differences (Breville vs Sage, the CLEAN ME vs CLEAN/DESCALE panels, DF54 UK buying) go in mustInclude, product names stay market-neutral, and the post never says 'we tested'.
contributionDetail gives the actual picker questions and their outcomes, so the toolsmith can build from it.
Owner reports are labelled as one person's experience, and reviewer measurements are attributed to the reviewer.
promptChanges: Before returning, check every titleOption: at most 70 characters with product names filled in, one promise, not a summary. Rewrite any that fail.
assets may contain only pickers or troubleshooters. If you want a diagram, photo or calculator, put that content into mustInclude as text, or make it a step of the troubleshooter.
Fetch each competitor page in this run. If a fetch fails, take the next search result. If a summary is based on the research artifact and not a page you opened now, say so in its summary.
The thesis must not contain anything your leaveOut bans (prices, unverified figures) or anything your mustInclude qualifies. Make the thesis exactly as strong as the evidence.
If another brief or existing guide already covers a diagnosis or test, reference it in one line (with {{guide:}} or the shared tool id) and don't restate its steps.
Don't ask the writer to verify facts. If a claim wasn't confirmed, drop it from claimIds and list it in leaveOut as unknown.
Search at least twice: once with the reader's question as written and once with forum-style wording, then pick the top 3 pages from both.
[niche] Home-Barista returns 403 to fetches. Don't count it as a reviewed competitor. Use Reddit r/espresso threads or CoffeeGeek for the forum perspective.
